fields: Sample quality control: genome build, bisulfite conversion, CpG coverage, specimen
The limits intake applies: conversion >= 0.98, opportunities >= 100,000. This is the rule the file must clear before the chain accepts it.

It accepts or refuses the sample file before anything else is read: checking that reads are aligned to hg19, that bisulfite conversion is at least 98%, and CpG coverage chromosome by chromosome, while recording the specimen. A damaged or incomplete file is refused with a stated reason.

Nothing downstream is read until the file passes, so the chain needs this gate to keep every later score from being built on a file with too little conversion, too few covered opportunities, the wrong genome build, or a bad specimen.
How it is obtained or computed

Computed by the chain from the sample's molecules and its references. The recorded test values are conversion_min: 0.98 and min_opportunities: 100000, alongside the hg19 alignment and chromosome-by-chromosome CpG coverage checks named in the instrument's own description.

law_part is 'not the law: a chain rule' and lf_section is 'not part of IAM's Law' — this check is not a term in IAM's Law. It is a rule-based threshold, computed by the chain from the sample's molecules and its references, used to gate intake rather than to express a regulating-energy cost.
Healthy value and how it is set
Healthy is conversion >= 0.98, with basis 'rule'; the recorded test values pairing with it are conversion_min: 0.98 and min_opportunities: 100000, and the check currently reads test_state: OK.

fields: Before any reading: the file must be readable and complete, on the hg19 build, with bisulfite conversion of at least 0.98, an accepted specimen word, at least 100,000 opportunities, and genome coverage on every chromosome. A failing file is refused with a plain reason (exit code 3, INTAKE_REFUSED), and no reading is shown.
A reading from a damaged, partial or wrong-build file would look like biology; refusing it plainly protects every instrument downstream.
The sample file; the specimen word; intake_thresholds_v2.json (Runtime Matrices/Intake).

(1) Limits are operational, not derived. (2) Specimen words decide the route (sorted, whole blood, plasma, tissue), not which cells are present.
